title: Write release notes from commits
what: Turns the commits since the last tag into release notes people can read: new features, fixes and anything that needs action when upgrading.
prompt:
Write release notes for the changes since the last release.

1. Find the latest tag with `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` (if there is none, use the first commit) and list commits since then with `git log <tag>..HEAD --no-merges`.
2. Sort them into: New, Improved, Fixed, and Breaking changes or action needed. Leave out internal chores, test-only and CI-only changes.
3. Write each item as one sentence a user would understand, not the commit message.
4. Suggest the next version number (semantic versioning) and say why.

Output Markdown only. Do not change any files or create tags.
cost: Low: reads commit messages and a few diffs.
